messages:
Ops-Bot: [ALERT] GPU OOM on prod-cluster-7 (node: infer-7b-12) detected at 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z. Headroom reported by allocator: 12%. Allocator failures x3. Creating incident thread.
Sanjay: ack, oncall here. any customer-facing errors?
Customer-Impact-Bot: Customer requests affected: 2 downstream realtime endpoints showing 502/timeout from inference-proxy between 11:59:50-12:00:20 UTC. Estimated requests impacted: ~120.
Alex: logs show CUDA error: "out of memory" inside runtime allocator while trying to reserve 256MB slab. Stack: runtime/allocator.cc:412 allocate_slab()
Maya: interesting — headroom=12% from headroom exporter, but allocator log shows reserve pool fragmented. paste logs?
Sanjay: pasting tail of node logs:
```
[12:00:00.123] INFO headroom_report: free=11.9% reserved=8.0% kv_cache_in_use=1.2%
[12:00:00.128] WARN allocator: reserve_block_claim failed id=0x7ff.. size=256MB reason=fragmentation
[12:00:00.129] ERR cuda: out of memory while allocating 268435456 bytes
[12:00:00.130] INFO prefetch: pending=4 inflight=2 last_prefetch=0.9s
```
Lee: that pattern looks like ghost reservations: headroom calc counts reserved blocks but fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation and we still show headroom.
Alex: agree. Also seeing deferred prefetches queue up. When prefetch requests are aggressive they end up reserving multiple small blocks causing holes.
Maya: impact: the node didn't OOM globally (there was free memory) but the allocator couldn't find contiguous slab for new model KV update. That matches "OOM despite headroom" pattern.
Sanjay: mitigation options? restart container, free KV cache, trigger slab compaction, or evict spare reserves. Which is fastest?
Alex: fastest immediate is to evict KV cache on the offending process to free contiguous space. Command: `curl -X POST http://infer-7b-12:9000/admin/kvcache/evict?percent=100`
Lee: caveat: evicting KV cache will increase latency for warm sessions (customer impact), but it's reversible.
Maya: I'm going to run the evict now on node infer-7b-12. Will also add a temporary denylist to prefetch config for this cluster to stop more prefetches.
Sanjay: go for it. tag me when done.
Maya: (runs) `POST /admin/kvcache/evict?percent=100` -> 200 OK. Response: evicted=34MB freed_contiguous=320MB.
Ops-Bot: action recorded: kvcache-evict executed by Maya at 2026-03-15T12:02:05Z.
Alex: nice, allocator now able to allocate slab. No further CUDA OOM errors in last 30s.
Customer-Impact-Bot: Customer endpoints recovered at ~12:02:20 UTC. Total impacted requests revised down to 95. Sending customer notif update?
Sanjay: yes — prepare a short note: transient OOM caused temporary 502s, mitigated by forced kvcache eviction and temporary prefetch throttle, no model state corruption, will follow with RCA.
Maya: did manual throttle: updated config `prefetch.max_inflight=1` for prod-cluster-7 via runtime-config service.
Lee: we need a durable mitigation: increase slab compaction frequency and expose contiguous-free metric. I can sketch a patch to the allocator to periodically coalesce free segments when fragmentation crosses threshold.
Alex: also consider reducing reservation granularity for prefetches (split large contiguous reserve into smaller chunk claims with compaction hints) — might reduce holes.
Sanjay: action items so far: 1) temp throttle prefetch (Maya) done; 2) kvcache-evict executed (Maya) done; 3) cordon node? not needed if stable, but keep oncall around (Sanjay). 4) implement telemetry for contiguous_free metric (Lee) assigned; 5) allocator compaction work (Alex) assigned.
Maya: leaving a diagnostic snapshot in /var/logs/incidents/3077770000/snapshot.log and uploading to infra-tools: `infractl upload snapshot infer-7b-12 /var/logs/incidents/3077770000/snapshot.log`
Ops-Bot: Deploy bot triggered: infractl upload completed (id: s-3077770000).
Sanjay: do we have any customer with high SLA who needs immediate outreach? Customer-Impact-Bot flagged customer "finpay" as high. Maya — can you add them to the status update?
Maya: yes — adding to message channel #status-updates. Draft: "We experienced a short period of elevated 502s due to GPU OOM on infer-7b-12. Mitigation applied and services recovered within ~2 minutes. No data loss. Follow-up RCA to be posted."
Lee: technical note for RCA: include allocator histogram: free_segments_count, largest_contiguous_free, reserved_fragments_count, kv_cache_slots. I'll attach the snapshot snippet:
```
allocator.metrics:
  total_free: 12.1%
  largest_contiguous_free: 287MB
  reserved_fragments_count: 14
  slab_compaction_runs_last_hour: 0
  kv_cache_pages: 129
```
Alex: interesting — largest_contiguous_free < slab request (256MB) + slack => borderline. After evict, largest_contiguous_free jumped to 610MB. So eviction was the right short-term fix.
Sanjay: next steps and owners: Lee -> add contiguous_free telemetry and alert rule if largest_contiguous_free < model_min_slab * 1.2; Alex -> trial compaction patch in staging; Maya -> revert prefetch throttle when we have a safe config; Ops-Bot -> annotate incident with timeline.
Maya: I'm also going to add a temporary automated response to prevent auto-retries from hammering the node while it's degrading: set retry.backoff=5s for the cluster proxy for 10m.
Alex: also file a targeted test: simulate fragmentation by creating many small reservations to validate compaction algorithm. I'll put test plan in the incident board.
Customer-Impact-Bot: Notified customers: finpay (high), three medium customers; initial status update posted to #status-updates at 12:06 UTC.
Sanjay: thanks all. Keeping thread open for the RCA drafts. If we get re-occurrence, escalate to cordon + reboot plan. For now we mark incident as mitigated.
Ops-Bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Time to mitigation: 2m 5s. Recording participants: Sanjay, Maya, Alex, Lee.
Maya: adding final note: short-term risk: if prefetch patterns resume, similar fragmentation can reoccur — we should consider defaulting prefetch to conservative behavior for all prod clusters until compaction lands.
Lee: logging follow-up: create ticket INF-4523 "allocator: contiguous-free telemetry and compaction" and attach snapshots.
Alex: I'll start the compaction PR draft.
Sanjay: closing oncall shift notes: action owners assigned, customer notified. If no further errors in 1h I'll close the incident.
Customer-Impact-Bot: Incident update: mitigated -> customers notified -> follow-up RCA planned.
Ops-Bot: thread closed by Ops-Bot at 2026-03-15T12:14:10Z (will auto-archive in 7 days).
